Abstract— As a preliminary study of unconstrained sleep 
monitoring, we developed the pillow insertion type module to 
measure the acceleration and pressure variation from the head 
movement during sleep. Result s of the pilot test show that the 
respiration activity could be extracted from the acceleration as 
well as the pressure variation. However, discriminating of the 
snoring and respiration has not performed in this configuration. 
I.   UNCONSTRAINED SLEEP MONITORING 
Sleep apnea and snoring are the representative sleep 
disorder. These could degrade the sleep quality, and moreover 
it could destroy the body balance that causes difficulty 
concentrating, fatigue and memory loss. Finally, it also causes 
not only the aggravation of daily life but also cardiovascular 
disease and unexpected dea th during sleep in severe cases. 
Polysomnography(PSG) is a representative method in sleep 
analysis. However, more convenient methods are still required 
because the PSG is expensive and needs complex preparation. 
Therefore, several unconstrained sleep monit oring methods 
has been introduced. For example, respiratory activity 
monitoring using pressure sensitive textile [1], ultrasound[2], 
optical fiber[3] or wireless signal[4] have been proposed as a 
comfortable sleep monitoring method. In this paper, we 
suggest another unconstrained sleep monitoring method based 
on the pillow insertion type standalone module that includes 
accelerometer and pressure sensor. 
II.   FEASIBILITY TEST AND RESULTS 
Developed module includes the 3-axis accelerometer 
(ADXL335, Analog Device, MA, USA) and the force-sensing 
resistor, FSR-406 (Interlin k Electronics, CA, USA) , to 
measure acceleration and pressure derived by the respiratory 
activity. Low power microprocessor MSP430 was used to 
record and transfer measured signal. To validate the developed 
system, experiment was performed in actual sleep condition. 
Developed module was inserted into the latex pillow, and the 
FSR-406 is attached to the module face down . To record 
reference respiration, microphone was installed 5 cm over the 
nose. Subject who has the snoring was participated to the 
experiment. Every sensor data was recorded with 40 Hz 
sampling frequency except on the microphone. Figure 2 shows 
an example of the recorded signal after 40-tap moving 
averaging. In FSR and x- and y-axis cases, n umbers of
